In normal conditions, what time gap should you keep behind the vehicle ahead?
Use the 2-second rule in normal conditions.
What following gap is recommended on a wet or slippery road?
Increase the normal gap to 4 seconds when conditions are poor.
If another driver is tailgating you, what is the safer response?
Increase your gap ahead and let them pass when safe
A larger gap ahead gives both drivers more time to react.
A posted speed limit tells you…
The target speed in every condition
The maximum legal speed in good conditions
The speed only trucks must use
You may need to drive more slowly when conditions or hazards require it.
A school bus has stopped to pick up children. What maximum speed applies while you pass?
Drive at 20 km/h or less until you are well past the bus.
Does the 20 km/h rule for a stopped school bus apply to traffic approaching from either direction?
Only to traffic behind the bus
The reduced speed applies no matter which direction you approach from.
At the bottom of a T-intersection, who must you give way to?
Nobody if there is no sign
Traffic on the terminating road gives way to traffic on the continuing road.
You are turning right and an oncoming vehicle is turning left. Who gives way?
A driver turning right gives way to oncoming traffic, including traffic turning left.
If no other give-way rule applies at an uncontrolled intersection, give way to…
The fallback rule is to give way to traffic from your right.
When entering a roundabout, you must give way to vehicles that…
Will cross your path from the right
Give way to vehicles already on the roundabout or entering from a road to your right.
When driving straight through a roundabout, when should you signal?
Do not signal at any time
Signal left after passing the exit before yours
Do not signal on approach; signal left as you pass the exit before the one you will take.
How long should you normally signal before turning or changing lanes?
Give other road users at least 3 seconds of warning.
What does a steady red traffic signal mean?
Proceed if no traffic is visible
What should you do at a yellow traffic signal?
Stop unless you are too close to stop safely
Treat it as a green signal
Stop only if pedestrians are present
A yellow signal means stop unless stopping safely is no longer possible.
Traffic signals are flashing yellow. What should you do?
Flashing yellow means the signals are not working; use the give-way rules.
When you give way, the other road user should not need to…
Stop, brake, swerve or take evasive action
Giving way means allowing the other road user to continue without evasive action.
